NONE: › an amount of money that is returned to you, especially by the government, for example when you have paid too much tax
（尤指政府返還的）部分退款

example: a tax rebate
退還部分稅款

NONE: B2 a person who is opposed to the political system in their country and tries to change it using force
（試圖武裝推翻國家政治制度的）反抗者，造反者
B2 to fight against the government
武力反抗；造反；反叛
› to refuse to obey rules or people in authority
叛逆；反叛
› to react against a feeling, action, plan, etc.
嫌惡；生反感；受不住
› a person who does not like rules or authority, and shows this by behaving differently from most people in society
（對抗權威或社會的）叛逆者

example: The rebels took over the capital and set up a new government.
叛亂分子佔領了首都並成立了新政府。
He was a rebel when he was a teenager and dyed his hair pink.
他十幾歲的時候有些叛逆，把頭髮染成了粉紅色。
The people rebelled against the harsh new government.
人民起來反抗這個殘暴的新政府。
If you are too strict with teenagers, they often rebel.
如果你對青少年太嚴厲，他們往往會反叛。
My poor sick stomach rebelled at the idea of any more food.
我的胃不太好，連想到食物都會反胃。

NONE: C1 violent action organized by a group of people who are trying to change the political system in their country
反叛，造反；叛亂
› action against those in authority, against the rules, or against normal and accepted ways of behaving
叛逆；抗爭；反抗

example: The government has brutally crushed the rebellion.
政府殘酷鎮壓了叛亂。
a backbench rebellion against the new foreign policy
後座議員對新外交政策的反對
her teenage rebellion
她青春期的叛逆行為

NONE: › If a group of people are rebellious, they oppose the ideas of the people in authority and plan to change the system, often using force.
（常使用武力）反叛的，造反的，反抗的
C1 If someone is rebellious, they are difficult to control and do not behave in the way that is expected.
桀驁不馴的；難以控制的；難對付的

example: Her teachers regard her as a rebellious, trouble-making girl.
老師們認為她是一個不服管教、惹是生非的女孩子。

NONE: › a new period of growth of something, or a time when something that was popular in the past becomes popular again
再生；復活；復興

example: English drama has enjoyed a rebirth since the 1950s with writers like John Osborne, Harold Pinter and Tom Stoppard.
自從20世紀50年代以來，隨著約翰．奧斯本、哈羅德．品特和湯姆．斯托帕德等劇作家的湧現，英國戲劇復興了。

NONE: › (of a computer) to switch off and then start again immediately, or to make a computer do this
（使）重新啟動（電腦）
› to start something again or do something again, in a way that is new and interesting
以新鮮有趣的方式重做

example: If this doesn't work, close the application and reboot the system.
如果這不解決問題，那麼關閉程式，重啟系統。
I'm just waiting for my laptop to reboot.
我只是在等我的筆記型電腦重啟。
With his new movie he reboots the classic Western.
他新拍的電影重新啟動了經典的西部片。

NONE: › existing or active again
再度出現；再度活躍
› having decided to accept a particular type of evangelical Christianity, especially after a deep spiritual experience
（尤指在深度精神體驗後，決定接受某一派別的基督教）重生的
› to be born again
再生的；復活的
› to start to exist or to become active again
再度開始；再度出現；再度活躍
› to decide to accept a particular type of evangelical Christianity, especially after a deep spiritual experience
（尤指在深度精神體驗後，決定接受某一派別的基督教）重生

example: a reborn version of a 1978 series
1978年的系列劇的重拍版本
Synonym
born-again
They believe that people are reborn after death.
他們相信人們死後會複生。
The old abandoned buildings have been reborn.
這座廢棄的老房子獲得了新生。

NONE: › to bounce back after hitting a hard surface
彈回；反彈；跳回
› If an action rebounds on you, it does not have the effect you hoped for but has an unpleasant effect on you instead.
産生事與願違的結果；適得其反
› to rise in price after a fall
（價格）反彈
› the act of rebounding
彈回；反彈；跳回
› in sports, a ball or puck (= small, round, hard object used in ice hockey) that becomes available after an unsuccessful attempt to score, or an occasion when this happens
（體育比賽中）試圖得分未成功之後的反彈球
› in basketball, an occasion when a player successfully gets the ball after a shot (= attempt to score) has been missed
（籃球比賽中）成功搶得投籃未中之後的反彈球

example: His continual demands for sympathy rebounded on him because his friends finally stopped listening.
他沒完沒了地希望從別人那裡得到同情，結果卻適得其反，因為最終他的朋友們都不願再聽他訴苦。
Cotton rebounded from declines early in the day to end at a higher price.
棉花價格在今天較早時下跌之後反彈收高。
I hit the ball on the rebound (= after it had hit the wall or ground once).
球反彈回來時被我擊中了。
Over three games he averaged 14.0 points and 8.7 rebounds.
三場比賽中他平均每場得分14.0分，獲反彈球8.7個。

NONE: › to change the way that an organization, company, or product is seen by the public
給（機構，公司，產品等）重塑形象

example: Businesses may decide to rebrand for several reasons.
企業可能因為種種原因而重塑形象。
We'll show you how to rebrand your organization in ten easy stages.
我們會向你們展示如何通過十個簡單步驟重塑公司形象。

NONE: › the act of changing the way that an organization, business company, or product appears to the public
給（機構，公司，產品等）重塑形象

example: a major corporate rebranding
大規模的公司形象重塑活動
As a part of the rebranding process they hoped to reposition the brand as the "original" travel company.
作為重塑形象的一部分，他們希望把公司重塑為「原創性」的旅遊公司。

NONE: › to refuse to accept a helpful suggestion or offer from someone, often by answering in an unfriendly way
粗暴拒絕；生硬拒絕；斷然拒絕

example: She rebuffed all suggestions that she should resign.
她斷然拒絕了所有勸她辭職的建議。

NONE: B1 to build something again that has been damaged or destroyed
重建；改建；使恢復原狀
B2 If you rebuild a system or organization, you develop it so that it works effectively.
重新組織；改造
B2 to try to return to the good situation that you were in before an unpleasant event happened to you
恢復正常的生活；重新安排生活

example: The cathedral was completely rebuilt in 1425 after it had been destroyed by fire.
這座大教堂毀於火災，於1425年得以全面重建。
Before the election, the party claimed it would rebuild the country's economy.
在大選前，這個政黨聲稱自己會重振國家經濟。
Many people have difficulty in rebuilding their lives when they come out of prison.
很多人在出獄後很難重新過正常的生活。

NONE: › to speak angrily to someone because you disapprove of what they have said or done
斥責；指責；訓斥

example: I was rebuked by my manager for being late.
我因為遲到而遭到經理的訓斥。

NONE: › to argue that a statement or claim is not true
反駁；駁斥；駁回

example: She has rebutted charges that she has been involved in any financial malpractice.
面對指控，她反駁說她沒有參與任何金融營私舞弊案。

NONE: › a statement that says that something is not true
反駁；駁回；駁斥

example: She issued a point-by-point rebuttal of the company's accusations.
她就公司的指控進行了針鋒相對的駁斥。
